critical_code_review_comments: SedutaLogsSection.jsx:141 — key `${p.user_name || 'anon'}-${p.join_time || i}` still falls back to array index when both user_name and join_time are missing; acceptable because Daily.co snapshots always provide at least user_name in practice, but if you want fully deterministic keys consider using participant session_id when present.

PrivacyUtentePage.jsx:184 — key `${h.timestamp}-${h.consent_type}-${h.action}` assumes (timestamp, consent_type, action) is unique. If two grants for the same consent_type happen within the same second (unlikely but possible with programmatic toggles), React will still warn. Consider adding a server-side id to consent history entries for full uniqueness.

The 4 eslint-disable-next-line comments on dangerouslySetInnerHTML are correctly placed above the JSX line and reference sanitizeHtml → safe from XSS. Good practice: also add a repo-level ESLint override or a small comment convention doc so future contributors know DOMPurify sanitization is required.
